packages.title: «Como el teléfono» reads the phone again, not the app's language
brief: UX-1649 (S2), regression R1D-1 from P186 (verify-b5-r1-D). What the last round did: P186 applies Idioma as Android's per-app language (`AppLanguageBridge.apply`, `App/lib/services/app_language.dart`), and the channel answers with the phone's own language tags on API 33+, kept in the static `AppLanguageBridge.phoneLocales`. Only the Idioma sheet's «Como el teléfono» subtitle reads them (`App/lib/widgets/language_selector.dart:84-90`). Why it fails: under a per-app language Flutter's locales are the app's (for example `en-ES` on a Spanish phone with Idioma English), and three places that mean "the phone" still read `platformDispatcher.locales`. `RegionalMaterialDelegate` (`App/lib/main.dart:436-438`; `App/lib/l10n/region.dart:131-147`) takes `firstDayOfWeekIndex` and the system clock's shape from that locale, so «Primer día de la semana: Como el teléfono» turns Monday into Sunday (Material `en`). The recognizer's region (`App/lib/services/native_speech.dart:197`) and the background reminder copy (`App/lib/services/reminder_copy.dart:26`, `:35`) do the same. Inferred from code; the device check below confirms it.

(a) `App/lib/services/app_language.dart`: back `phoneLocales` with a static `ValueNotifier<List<Locale>?>` (for example `static final phone = ValueNotifier<List<Locale>?>(null);`), keeping a static getter and setter named `phoneLocales` over it, so `language_selector.dart:88` and ux-tester's tests keep working. Add one helper, `static List<Locale> phoneOr(List<Locale> flutter) => phoneLocales ?? flutter;`, and use it everywhere below. When `apply` gets a non-empty answer, also save the tags (the strings as received, in order) on the device: one row in the existing `app_preferences` table, scope `phone-locales`, data a JSON list, written the way `RegionalPreferenceStore.write` writes its row (`App/lib/providers/regional_provider.dart:126-134`). Add a small `readSavedPhoneLocales([TaskDatabase?])` beside it that returns the parsed locales (with the existing `_locale` parser) or null when there is no row or it can't be read. This stores a copy of a phone setting on the phone only, is never sent anywhere, and adds no setting. When `apply` answers null or empty (below Android 13), write nothing.

(b) `App/lib/main.dart`: in `main()`, read the saved tags in the same `Future.wait` as `appearance.ready` and `regional.ready` (:54) and seed `AppLanguageBridge.phoneLocales` with them, so the first frame already uses the phone's week start; `apply` in `initState` (:95) then replaces them with the fresh answer. In `build`, pass `AppLanguageBridge.phoneOr(WidgetsBinding.instance.platformDispatcher.locales).firstOrNull ?? const Locale('en')` as `RegionalMaterialDelegate`'s device locale (:436-438), and use `phoneOr(...)` for `locale: regional.localeFor(...)` (:429-431) too. Leave `localeListResolutionCallback` (:432-433) as it is. Rebuild when the answer arrives: listen to `AppLanguageBridge.phone` in `initState` and call `setState` (remove the listener in `dispose`), or wrap the `MaterialApp` in a `ValueListenableBuilder`; `RegionalMaterialDelegate.shouldReload` (`region.dart:157-161`) already reloads when `deviceLocale` changes.

(d) `App/lib/services/reminder_copy.dart`: in `readReminderStrings` (:26) and `readReminderCopy` (:35), when `deviceLocales` is null, use `AppLanguageBridge.phoneLocales`, then the saved tags (`readSavedPhoneLocales(database)`), then `PlatformDispatcher.instance.locales`. A background isolate starts with `phoneLocales` null, so the saved row is what it reads. Keep the `deviceLocales` parameter exactly as it is; tests pass it.

Don't re-apply the language on `didChangeLocales`: `setApplicationLocales` raises its own locale change, and a loop is worse than a phone-language change while the app is open being picked up at the next start. Don't touch: `AppLanguageBridge.kt` (it already answers with the phone's tags), what Idioma itself sets, the clock and week-start sheets on Hora y región, the capture language rules beyond the `devices` argument. No copy changes.
acceptance: Widget test, Android target, Flutter's locales set to `en-ES`, the `taskflow/app-language` channel answering `['es-ES']`, Idioma English, «Primer día de la semana: Como el teléfono»: once the answer arrives, `MaterialLocalizations.of(context).firstDayOfWeekIndex` in the app is 1 (Monday), without any other rebuild trigger.
Same setup with the `phone-locales` row already saved as `['es-ES']` and the channel not yet answered: the first frame already has `firstDayOfWeekIndex` 1.
Phone `en-US`, Idioma Español, week start «Como el teléfono»: `firstDayOfWeekIndex` is 0 (Sunday), the phone's, not Spanish Monday.
Below Android 13 (the channel answers null) and off Android: `phoneOr` returns Flutter's locales, nothing is saved, and every existing regional and language test passes unchanged.

Unit: with the `phone-locales` row saved as `['es-ES']`, `phoneLocales` null and `PlatformDispatcher` locales `en-ES`, `readReminderCopy(database, system24Hour: true)` resolves its device locale to `es-ES` (Idioma «Como el teléfono» gives Spanish copy).
`captureSpeechLanguage` gets the bridge's phone locales as `devices` when they are set.
deviceChecks: Emulator lane, Android 13+: phone in Spanish (Spain), Idioma English, week start «Como el teléfono»: Calendar's week strip starts on Monday; switch Idioma back to «Como el teléfono»: still Monday, in Spanish.
Emulator lane: with the same setup, let a reminder fire from the background (app swiped away): its text is in English and its time reads the way the app shows it.

packages.title: Recordatorios: after turning on, Detalles waits for the alerts and shows a failed refresh
brief: UX-1650 (S2), regression R1D-2 from P187 (verify-b5-r1-D). What the last round did: for UX-1605, `turnOnReminders` (`App/lib/widgets/reminder_control.dart:120`) shows «Listo. Recordatorios activados.» without waiting and runs `access.reconcile(owner)` unawaited, with `.catchError` recording `refresh_failed` (:189-196); `_turnOn` (`App/lib/screens/notification_settings_screen.dart:131-152`) then calls `_load(refresh: false)`. Why it fails: that load reads `upcomingAlerts` and `schedulingInfo` before the background reconcile has written them, so «Próximos avisos» shows «No hay próximos avisos. Elige un recordatorio en una tarea con fecha.» or an old list, and a `refresh_failed` never reaches «Reintentar» until the next resume. Verified in code.

Fix: the screen waits for the same reconcile, not a second one (`access.reconcile` isn't queued, `App/lib/services/notification_service.dart:442-446`, so a second `_load()` with the refresh would run two at once). (a) Give `turnOnReminders` an optional named parameter, `void Function(Future<void> scheduling)? onScheduling`, and hand it the very future passed to `unawaited` (the `reconcile(...).catchError(...)` chain, so it completes after `refresh_failed` is recorded). The other callers (`reminder_ask_sheet.dart:116`, `reminder_control.dart:404`, `:508`) pass nothing and behave exactly as today. (b) In `_turnOn`, capture that future. When `on` is true and a future was handed over, keep `_busy` and `_turningOn` true until it completes, so the switch stays on, the problem block stays hidden and the existing `LinearProgressIndicator` (:245) shows the wait; then set `_busy` false and call `_load(refresh: false)`, then clear `_turningOn` as today. When `on` is false, keep today's path (the switch and the problem come back at once). Resume during the wait still only re-reads the capability (:58).

Don't touch: the confirmation's timing (it must still show before the reconcile completes, UX-1605's acceptance), the problem block's copy and buttons (UX-1606), the alarms sheet (UX-1622), `reminder_ask_sheet.dart`. No copy changes.
acceptance: Widget test, ES, Recordatorios, a fake access whose `reconcile` completes 2 s after the turn-on and then has one upcoming alert stored: «Listo. Recordatorios activados.» shows before it completes; until it completes the switch is on, the progress bar shows and no «El teléfono no deja que TaskFlow te avise.» line appears; after it completes, with Detalles expanded, the alert's row shows and «No hay próximos avisos. Elige un recordatorio en una tarea con fecha.» doesn't.
Same, with a reconcile that fails: after it ends, «Reintentar» shows, without any app lifecycle resume.
`reconcile` runs once per turn-on from Recordatorios (no second run from `_load`).
A refusal at Android's dialog still turns the switch off and brings the problem line back at once, as UX-1605's test checks.
The existing UX-1605 test «Listo. Recordatorios activados.» with a `reconcile` that never completes still passes.
deviceChecks: Emulator lane: re-capture `permission-alarms.allowed` after allowing, then open Detalles once the bar ends: the upcoming alerts are listed.

packages.title: Follow-ups on three settings screens: one button under the calendars, an instant scroll with animations off, the name read as a heading
brief: UX-1651 (S2), regression R1D-3 from P188 (verify-b5-r1-D; render `App/build/ux/first-run/phone-calendars.allowed.es.light.1x.png`). What the last round did: for UX-1611 it moved «Ocultar eventos del calendario» (`calendarDisable`) below the calendars list as a TextButton. Why it fails: it now sits under «Borrar selección» (`calendarClear`), a centred TextButton of the same colour, with only «Actualizar calendarios» between them, and both leave Calendar with no phone events. Fix (subtract): in `App/lib/screens/device_calendars_screen.dart:133-138`, remove the `if (state.preferences.selected.isNotEmpty) TextButton(... calendarClear)` block. «Ocultar eventos del calendario» covers showing none, and each row's checkbox covers one calendar; the controls below the list go from 3 to 2. Remove `calendarClear` and `@calendarClear` from `app_en.arb`, `app_es.arb` («Borrar selección») and `app_ca.arb` («Esborra la selecció»), then `flutter gen-l10n`. Keep `clearSelection` in `device_calendar_provider.dart` (its provider test, `device_calendar_test.dart:222`, stays); only the button goes. Re-render `first-run/phone-calendars.allowed` (ES 1× and 2×).

UX-1612 (S2), second attempt; the first got the slogan half right (`App/lib/screens/account_screen.dart:184-193`: the first name in `headlineMedium` above the email, or the email first; `accountHeading` gone). What's left for this finding: the name is drawn as a heading but TalkBack doesn't hear it as one (AUDIT `settings/account · named`). Wrap the name's `Text` (:186) in `Semantics(header: true, child: ...)`. The name row and the name sheet are UX-1515's, in P194 (D5): add no row here, and don't change the email line.

UX-1652 (S1), regression R1D-4 from P188 (verify-b5-r1-D). What the last round did: for UX-1620 `_revealMessage` scrolls the result banner into view with two `Scrollable.ensureVisible` calls of 250 ms (`App/lib/screens/data_transfer_screen.dart:62-70`). Why it fails: the scroll animates even with Android's «Quitar animaciones» on. Fix: read `MediaQuery.disableAnimationsOf` from the banner's context (it is mounted at that point) and pass `Duration.zero` when it's true, `const Duration(milliseconds: 250)` otherwise, as `day_timeline_screen.dart:136` does. Keep the two alignment policies and the `jumpTo` steps above them.

Don't touch: the phone calendars' lead lines, «Conectar», «Actualizar calendarios», the first-connection selection (D7); Cuenta's email line and P194's future row; the import and export themselves and the banner's copy.
acceptance: ES at 1× and 2× on 360×800, `first-run/phone-calendars.allowed` with every calendar ticked: below the list there is one TextButton, «Ocultar eventos del calendario», and the outlined «Actualizar calendarios»; «Borrar selección» doesn't appear in any state; no catalog contains `calendarClear`.
Cuenta, ES, an account with first name «María»: the semantics node «María» is a header; an account without a name: no node in the screen's body is a header (the app bar's title aside).

Exportar e importar with `MediaQueryData(disableAnimations: true)`: after an import result, the banner is fully in view one frame later, with no scroll frames in between; with animations on, the reveal still animates.
deviceChecks: Emulator lane, TalkBack, ES: on Cuenta, the name is announced as a heading («María, encabezado»).
Emulator lane, «Quitar animaciones» on: an import's result banner jumps into view.
